title: Pharmacokinetics Clinical Ward
learning_goals: Master laboratory personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements.
Accurately tare and weigh medicinal powders on an analytical digital balance.
Perform aseptic dissolution and rigorous sample labelling.
Administer oral pharmacotherapy and monitor plasma concentration dynamics.
Conduct timed venous sampling and clinical centrifuge/fluorescence assays.
Segregate biomedical and chemical waste according to safety standards.

rules.text: Protective safety goggles must be equipped before handling active drugs or chemicals.
rules.hint: Don complete personal protective equipment (coat, goggles, gloves) before ward duties.

rules.text: Chemical-resistant gloves must be worn before manipulating hazardous reagents or specimens.
rules.hint: Equip nitrile gloves to protect hands during medication handling and biological sampling.

rules.text: Buttoned laboratory coat required before beginning experiments in active lab zones.
rules.hint: Fasten laboratory coat to protect against biological specimen and chemical contact.

rules.text: Analytical digital balance must be tared to zero with container in place prior to weighing samples.
rules.hint: Zero digital balance before placing powder boat to measure net sample weight.

rules.text: All beakers, vials, and solutions must be explicitly labeled with contents and concentration.
rules.hint: Label dosing cup with patient nickname, drug name, and exact administered dose.

rules.text: Always add acid to water slowly; never pour water directly into concentrated reagents.
rules.hint: Follow safe solution handling protocol when reconstituting and preparing oral medications.

rules.text: Rinse burette with titrant and never exceed graduated volumetric capacity.
rules.hint: Allow sufficient simulated elapsed time after dose for absorption before blood collection.

rules.text: Administered medication dose must not exceed safe therapeutic threshold.
rules.hint: Prescribe within adult clinical dose bounds (e.g. 500mg-1000mg for paracetamol).

rules.text: Chemical, biological, and sharps waste must be disposed into designated segregated waste receptacles.
rules.hint: Place used phlebotomy sharps and blood tubes into the rigid biohazard container.

rules.text: Decontaminate hands and remove PPE in proper aseptic sequence before exiting laboratory.
rules.hint: Remove contaminated PPE carefully and scrub hands at ward hygiene sink.

wear_ppe: Put on all required PPE (safety goggles, lab gloves, and lab coat).
tare_balance: Tare the analytical balance with the empty weighing dish first.
weigh_powder: Weigh a safe therapeutic dose of paracetamol powder (e.g. 500 mg).
dissolve_dose: Dissolve the weighed drug powder into water inside the dosing cup.
label_cup: Label the dosing cup with patient ID and medication info.
administer_oral: Administer the prepared oral medication to the patient.
advance_time: Advance simulated time (e.g. 1.0 h) to allow gastrointestinal absorption.
label_tube: Label a blood collection tube before performing the venous draw.
draw_blood: Draw a sterile venous blood sample from the patient into the tube.
run_assay: Load the blood sample into the centrifuge/assay analyzer to measure plasma level.
dispose_waste: Dispose of biomedical waste (used tubes, needles) into the biohazard bin.
wash_hands: Remove PPE and wash hands thoroughly at the sink.
submit_report: Submit the completed pharmacokinetics clinical ward report.

common_mistakes.remedy: Always press tare with the container on the balance before weighing drug powder.
Single doses of paracetamol must not exceed 1000 mg to prevent hepatotoxicity.
